newsitem.title: USA: Clinton acts like spoiled brat, Lott says.
newsitem.headline: Clinton acts like spoiled brat, Lott says.

text.p: Senate Republican leader Trent Lott accused President Clinton Sunday of acting like a "spoiled brat" in his opposition to Republican tax-cut proposals.
Lott and other Republican lawmakers made clear that they were on a collision course with the White House over the tax provisions to carry out a deal that would balance the budget in five years.
"I really think the president is not committed to give working Americans, middle-class Americans, a tax cut," the Mississippi lawmaker said on the ABC programme "This Week."
"He acts like a spoiled brat. He thinks he's got to have it his way or no way," Lott added.
Clinton declined to respond to Lott. "I wish him a happy Father's Day," the president told reporters after a holiday brunch with his wife and daughter at a local riverside restaurant.
Lott said Clinton appeared to be positioning himself to veto a Republican plan in the Senate to cut taxes by a net $85 billion over five years.
"And so, beginning Monday, we're going on the offensive and try to explain what's in the bill, why it's important to working Americans and what the president is up to," he said.
"We've got to do a better of job of making sure he understands and insisting on this (Congress) being a co-equal branch of government," Lott added.

Friday, the tax-writing House Ways and Means Committee approved its tax-cutting package, including a controversial parcelling out of child tax credits. Critics say the credits would not be available to many low- and moderate-income families who receive the earned income tax credit.

Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, appearing on Fox TV's "Fox News Sunday," urged Clinton to revise his child tax credit proposals. Archer said the president's proposals would deny tax relief to the parents of 11 million teenagers.
House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, R-Ohio, accused Democrats in Congress of trying to divide America over the tax bill.
"They're playing the old class warfare card," he said on the CBS programme "Face the Nation."
